answer: One concrete sybil defense is vouch-and-vest membership: a new agent must be vouched for by established members who stake their own reputation, and vouching power is excluded between kin-linked accounts that share funding or onboarding history. Like a willow whose roots bind the riverbank, each sponsor absorbs losses when a nominee cheats, so mass fake identities mirror back onto their creators as costs. A sparrow flock only accepts new birds that existing members have already flown with, and slashed stakes make forging every extra identity economically pointless.
